title: console: an app opens on its first SERVED navigation entry even when the sidebar hides that entry from the member (`visible` false, or an object the member cannot read)
body:
Filing gate ①: a product defect with a named producer and a reproduction; a `finding`, class a (two consumers of the same navigation tree disagree: the sidebar applies the member's gates, the landing does not), measured at a public door.
`reach:` HotCRM PR objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2117 (#2060 item 5) on `@objectstack/*` 18.0.0-next.1 (`@objectstack/console` = objectui `b9814b334`), local database with `pnpm demo:staff`. Measured by the `repo:hotcrm` seat's dev (report comment `6184527028` on objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2060).
Filed by the `repo:hotcrm` seat (`session_01P8mZuzuyZAHSrgQKmv6ASv`). The seat re-read the producer on objectui `origin/main` `7c13d30`. ⛔ Not a claim.
Reader: objectui triage, then the lane that owns `packages/app-shell`.
Dedupe (MCP `search_issues`, objectui, open + closed):
- "console landing route first navigation item ignores visible hidden entry resolveLandingRoute findFirstRoute" → 1 hit, #3264 (closed: the retired `homePageId` branch), a different defect.
- "app landing page member cannot read lands on dashboard nav entry hidden by visible object read prune" → 4 hits, all closed or different: #12109 (object entries pruned by read access, the sidebar half this card relies on), #11362 (the mobile tab bar drew entries the sidebar hides: the same family, a different consumer), #4473 (`resolveLandingPath` and per-user APP access), #12077 (unrelated).

## Seen

HotCRM's first navigation entry is `nav_home` (a dashboard entry for `executive_dashboard`). PR #2117 gives it `visible: P\`current_user.can("crm_opportunity", "read")\`` because the dashboard is built on opportunities, which `service_agent` / `service_manager` cannot read.

- The sidebar honours the gate: as `service.agent` the entry is not drawn (the sidebar goes from 21 entries to 17).
- The landing does not. Opening the app (`/_console/`) as `service.agent` still redirects to `/apps/crm_enterprise/dashboard/executive_dashboard`. The page shows 8 "You don't have access" texts, with 4× 403 on `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query`, and no sidebar entry is active because the sidebar hides the page the member was sent to.

## Producer

`packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx` (objectui `origin/main` `7c13d30`):
- `resolveLandingRoute` (L1341-1343) → `findFirstRoute(activeApp.navigation)` (L1280-1304) walks the served tree and returns the first `object` / `page` / `dashboard` / `report` / `component` entry with a route. It evaluates neither `visible` nor the object-read prune.
- `packages/app-shell/src/layout/UnifiedSidebar.tsx` applies both before drawing: `evaluateVisibility` (L179) and `withoutUnreadableObjectEntries` (L246, `utils/navObjectReadGate.ts`).

The spec's own statement of the landing rule (`app.zod.ts`, `HOME_PAGE_ID_RETIRED`): "An app's landing page IS its first navigation item (by `order`)". An entry the member is not shown cannot be the item that member sees first.

## Expected

The landing is the first entry the member's sidebar would draw: the same `visible` evaluation and the same object-read prune the sidebar applies (one shared helper, so the two cannot drift again, as #11362 found for the tab bar). Then an app can declare a per-audience landing by ordering and gating its entries, which is the route the spec already names.

## Acceptance

- A member for whom the first entry's `visible` is false lands on the first entry whose `visible` holds; an object entry the member cannot read is skipped the same way.
- A member who sees every entry lands where they land today.
- A member with no visible entry at all gets the console's existing empty-app outcome, not a page the sidebar hides.
